plan.curriculum: Mathematics 2.0, Number, Year 6 (VC2M6N09): representing a budget in a spreadsheet, creating and using formulas to calculate totals
plan.shape: example-first: the teacher names cells and builds one formula, then the class predicts what formulas calculate, because cell references are new
plan.criticalFeature: a formula uses cell references (like B2), so the total updates itself when a number changes
decisionPoints: the choice check: which formula finds the cost of the pencils?
plan.anchor: read it, model it, solve it, check it: say what the answer means in the situation
plan.catchUp: Missed Sessions 1 or 2? Show a budget table: income minus expenses equals money left over.

studentTools: Devices with a spreadsheet program (Google Sheets or Excel), if available
Printed Worksheet for every student; Extension and Supported Worksheet as needed
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
boardSetup: The fortnight's anchor on the board: read it, model it, solve it, check it
If devices are available, open a blank spreadsheet on the board and type the I Do example live

resources.label: Worksheet
resources.description: Your turn. Name cells, predict formulas, build a camping budget, fix a formula, and change a number.
resources.title: Budgets in a Spreadsheet
resources.subtitle: A formula uses cell references, so totals update themselves.

example.prompt: In a shopping sheet, column B is Price and row 3 is Ruler. What is cell B3?
steps: Read the cell: the ruler's price.

items.prompt: A sheet of netball stats. Column A: player, B: goals, C: games. Fill in the missing cells.
B2 = 12, C2 = 5, D2 = 30. What does each formula show?
Kai typed a formula for the cost of the tents. Find his mistake and fix it.
work: Cost each is in B2, how many is in C2.
items.answer: He added instead of multiplying. It should be =B2*C2, which shows $90.

example.prompt: Write the formula for the torch total (row 4).
steps: Cost each is in B4, how many in C4.

items.prompt: The camping budget sheet: row 2 Tent ($45, 2), row 3 Sleeping bag ($28, 4), row 4 Torch ($12, 3). Write each formula for column D and its value.
Sleeping bags go on sale at $22. Which cells change by themselves?
items.explain: You type the new price in B3. D3 uses B3 and D5 adds D3, so both update: D3 = $88, D5 = $214.

resources.label: Extension
resources.description: Early finisher option. A discount formula, an average with formulas, and designing your own budget sheet, with worked examples.
resources.title: Extension: Spreadsheet Wizard
resources.subtitle: Formulas that use other formulas.

example.prompt: Price in B2 is $80. Write a formula for 25% off.

items.prompt: Price in B2. Write a formula for the price with 10% GST added.
Price in B3. Write a formula for 30% off. What does it show if B3 is $50?
A netball team's goals are in B2:B6: 14, 22, 18, 9, 17. What does each formula show?

example.prompt: Plan a sheet for a weekly budget.
steps: Column A: items. Column B: income. Column C: expenses.

items.prompt: Design a spreadsheet for your own weekly budget. Sketch the columns and rows, and write every formula you would use.
items.answer: Check: labelled columns, income and expense totals with SUM, and a left-over cell like =B10-C10.

resources.label: Supported Worksheet
resources.description: For students who need more guidance: reading cells first, then simple add and multiply formulas, with a hint on every question.
resources.title: Spreadsheets: Step by Step
resources.subtitle: Column letter first, then row number.

slides.notes: Session 3 of our budgeting week: today we put a budget into a spreadsheet.

Before you start, put boards and markers on every desk. If you have devices, open a blank spreadsheet on the board. Print the Worksheet for everyone, and a few copies of the Extension and the Supported Worksheet.

beats: SAY: Let's warm up with the four processes.
ASK: What is 12.45 plus 8.79?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: $21.24
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> line up the decimal points and regroup together. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The answer is 21.24.
Line up the points, then add. Tick it or fix it.
trap: misaligning the decimal points.
Fix: line up the points, and they add again.
notes.prep: Review of the four processes (the request named the focus). Keep the review under 6 minutes.

beats: ASK: What is 3 dollars 60 times 7?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: $25.20
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> split into $3 x 7 and 60c x 7, then add. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 3 times 7 is 21, and 60 cents times 7 is 4.20: 25.20.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing $21.42.
Fix: split 3.60 into 3 and 0.60, and they redo it.

beats: ASK: If 37.50 is shared by 5, how much does each get?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: $7.50
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then on to Fluency.
Less -> use the division bracket with cents. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 37.50 divided by 5 is 7.50 each. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing $7.05.
Fix: change to cents, 3750 divided by 5, and they redo it.

beats: SAY: Now for our nine times table.
Write each answer as fast as you can.
ASK: What is 9 times 9?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 81
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> 10 nines is 90, take one 9 away. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 81. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 72 or 89.
Fix: 10 nines is 90, take away 9, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Times tables fluency. Keep the whole block under 5 minutes.

beats: SAY: Here's the next one.
ASK: What is 9 times 4?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 36
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> 10 fours is 40, take one 4 away. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 36. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 32 or 45.
Fix: 10 fours is 40, take away 4, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Brisk: one line of feedback, then the next.

beats: SAY: Now a division. How many nines make 54?
ASK: What is 54 divided by 9?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 6
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the learning intention.
Less -> count up in nines to 54. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 6. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 5 or 7.
Fix: check: 6 nines is 54, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Brisk: one line of feedback, then the next.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to use a spreadsheet and formulas to calculate a budget.
successCriteria: I can find a cell using its column letter and row number.
I can write a formula that uses cell references to calculate a total.
I can explain why a spreadsheet total updates when a number changes.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: We've made budgets with pencil and paper.
Today we let a spreadsheet do the calculating.
SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: The first one is where we start,
and the second one is our big goal today.
notes.prep: SC1 cell names are reachable for everyone; SC2 writing a formula is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 explaining updates is the stretch.

slides.title: What changes?
slides.prompt: If pencils go up to $3, what else has to change?

notes.answer: the pencil cost and the total
beats: POINT to the price of pencils.
SAY: This is a shopping list in a spreadsheet: price, how many, and cost.
ASK: If pencils go up to 3 dollars,
what else has to change on this list? Tell your partner.
20 sec. Cue: Partner A first. You have 20 seconds. Go.
EXPECT: the pencil cost, and the total
SAY: On paper, we'd rub out and work out the cost and total again.
In a spreadsheet, a formula does that for us. That's today.
trap: saying only the price changes.
Fix: ask what 4 pencils cost now, and they look again.
notes.prep: The launch comes after the LI: why formulas are worth learning. Under 4 minutes.

slides.meaning: An instruction in a spreadsheet cell that calculates a value. It starts with =.
slides.example: =B2*C2 multiplies the numbers in cells B2 and C2.

beats: POINT to the word.
SAY: This word is formula. Say it with me: for-mu-la.
SAY: A formula is an instruction that tells a cell to calculate something.
It always starts with an equals sign, and it uses cell names like B2.
ASK: What sign does every formula start with?
5 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: =
trap: writing x for multiply.
Fix: say spreadsheets use a star for multiply, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: In spreadsheets, * means multiply and / means divide.

slides.title: Cells and formulas
steps: Every cell has a name: column letter, then row number.
B2 is the price of pencils: $2.50.

beats: POINT to column B, then row 2.
SAY: Every cell has a name: the column letter, then the row number.
This cell is B2, the price of pencils.
MODEL typing =B2*C2.
SAY: To find the cost, I type equals, B2, star, C2. The star means multiply.
The cell shows 10 dollars: 2.50 times 4.
ASK: What formula goes in D3 for the ruler, and what will it show?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: =B3*C3, $3.60
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: =B3*C3: 1.80 times 2 is 3.60.
Same formula, next row down.
trap: typing =1.80*2.
Fix: ask what happens if the price changes, and they use the cell names.
notes.stretch: What formula finds the glue stick cost?
notes.help: Point to the column, then the row, before writing.
notes.prep: The critical feature: cell references, not typed numbers. SC1 and SC2.

slides.title: Add up with SUM
steps: =SUM(D2:D4) adds every cell from D2 to D4.
Change a price, and the total changes by itself.

beats: POINT to D5.
SAY: For the total, I use SUM.
=SUM, D2 colon D4 means add every cell from D2 down to D4.
MODEL changing a price.
SAY: If I change the pencils to 3 dollars, D2 updates to 12,
and the total updates too. I don't redo anything.
ASK: What will D5 show before any change?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: $23.20
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
And after the pencil change it would show 25.20.
trap: adding the prices instead of the costs.
Fix: point to column D, and they redo it.
notes.stretch: What would D5 show if you bought 6 rulers?
notes.help: Add the D column one cell at a time.

slides.title: Which formula finds the pencil cost?
slides.prompt: Price in B2, how many in C2. Point to A, B or C

options.misconception: adds instead of multiplying price by how many
types numbers, so the formula won't update when a price changes

beats: SAY: Think: how do you find a cost? And what makes it update?
ASK: Which formula finds the cost of the pencils?
15 sec. Cue: Voices off. Point... now. Hold your point.
EXPECT: pointing to B
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then cold call one student: What's the problem with C?
Less -> say cost = price times how many, and point to the cells. Re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: It's B. A adds instead of multiplying.
C gives the right answer today, but won't update if the price changes.
trap: pointing to C.
Fix: ask what happens if the price changes, and they choose again.
notes.prep: First decision point. A: operation; C: typed numbers instead of references.

slides.title: What does it show?
slides.pivot: find each cell's value first, then do the operation
slides.followUp: cold call one board: Which cells did you use?

items.say: 84 divided by 6 is 14: the slash means divide.

say: Write what each one shows on your board.
trap: reading the column letter as the value.
Fix: point to the cell, read its number, and they redo it.
notes.stretch: Write a formula for each sheet that does something different.
notes.help: Write each cell's value under its name first.
notes.prep: Guided practice with multiply, SUM, subtract and divide. SC2.

beats: SAY: This one is just for you.
Read the formula in D5 carefully.
ASK: What will cell D5 show?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: $109
SCAN every board, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then Your turn.
Less -> point to D2, D3 and D4 together and add. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 50, 24 and 35 make 109 dollars. Tick it or fix it.
trap: adding the prices: $32.50.
Fix: point to column D, and they redo it.
notes.prep: The hinge before independent work. Anyone adding the prices starts on the Supported Worksheet with the teacher.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: Read, write and use spreadsheet formulas on your worksheet.

beats: POINT to the steps.
SAY: Read each question carefully, solve it carefully, then check your answers.
SAY: If you finish, the Extension is your early finisher option.
Let's read the steps together. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE and ask: Does your formula use cell names?
TIME: 20 minutes. Stop everyone once at 10 minutes to share a strategy.
trap: typing numbers into formulas.
Fix: ask what happens if a price changes, and they use cell names.
notes.stretch: Extension: discount formulas, averages, and your own budget sheet.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: reading cells first, then add and multiply formulas.
notes.prep: Independent practice: cell names, predicting formulas, a camping budget and a mistake. The sheet is evidence for SC2 and SC3.

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: Write the formula for D2, and say what it shows.

beats: SAY: Here's the last one. Work it out on your own board.
ASK: What formula goes in D2, and what will it show?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: =B2*C2, $52
RECORD who adds, or types numbers instead of cell names.
They start tomorrow's excursion budget with the teacher.
trap: writing =B2+C2.
Fix: none now. Record the name for tomorrow.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2: a new formula with cell references.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Tell your partner why spreadsheets use cell names in formulas.

notes.answer: open - listen for so totals update when a number changes
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How sure are you that you can write a spreadsheet formula?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit board.
A thumb up with =B2+C2 on the board matters most.
ASK: Why do formulas use cell names instead of numbers?
20 sec. Cue: Partner A first. You have 20 seconds. Go.
EXPECT: so totals update when a number changes
notes.prep: Read the self-assessment beside the exit evidence. Tomorrow: an excursion budget.
